title: Two Ends of a Long Country: Bratislava and Košice in a Split Week
subRegion: Bratislava (Staré Mesto, Petržalka, Devín) and Košice (Hlavná, Spiš)

bestPeriod.window: mid-May to late June, and September — terrace weather, no August closures, Košice before the student term crush
bestPeriod.avoid: late December (Bratislava's markets are lovely and the hotel rates are not) and January–February fog on the Danube

accommodation.note: €350–€630 (€50–€90/night; Košice is materially cheaper than Bratislava)

food.note: €175–€280 (€25–€40/day — Slovak restaurant prices remain low outside the Bratislava tourist core)

transport.note: €90–€150 (Vienna airport bus, the Bratislava–Košice IC train, two city transport passes)

hook: Slovakia is 430 km wide and its two cities have almost nothing in common. Bratislava is a Habsburg river town wedged against two borders, with a coronation cathedral, a Secession church the colour of a swimming pool, and Europe's densest concrete suburb across the Danube. Košice is a Gothic east-Slovak capital built along one enormous elongated square, with the easternmost Gothic cathedral in Europe at the top of it. Between them: a five-and-a-half-hour train and an entirely different country.

snapshot.Start / End: Bratislava (3 nights) → Košice (3 nights), fly out of Košice or return by train
snapshot.Getting there: **Fly to Vienna (VIE), not Bratislava.** The airport bus to Bratislava takes about an hour and runs many times a day, and Vienna's route network is incomparably better than BTS's. Košice (KSC) has flights to Vienna, Prague, Warsaw, London and Bratislava.

itinerary.title: Arrival and the Staré Mesto
itinerary.morning: Land at Vienna, take the airport coach to Bratislava — about an hour, several operators, arrivals at Most SNP or the main bus station [VERIFY: current Vienna airport–Bratislava coach fare and frequency]. Drop bags, buy an IDS BK multi-day pass.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk in through **Michael's Gate** and down Michalská to **Hlavné námestie** — the Roland Fountain, the Old Town Hall, and the French soldier leaning on the bench. Then the **Primate's Palace**, for the Hall of Mirrors and the six English **Mortlake tapestries** telling the story of Hero and Leander, found walled up in 1903 [VERIFY: current Primate's Palace hours and ticket].
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Modrá Hviezda** on Beblavého, on the climb to the castle — game, venison, dark beer, and the best traditional table in the old town.

itinerary.title: The Blue Church, the castle, the bridge
itinerary.morning: The **Blue Church** on Bezručova — Lechner's Church of St Elizabeth, 1913, blue from the plaster to the roof tiles to the pews. Opening is tied to the Mass schedule, so check the parish board and go early [VERIFY: current visiting hours outside services].
itinerary.afternoon: Up to **Bratislava Castle**, rebuilt after its 1811 fire and 20th-century ruin, housing the **Slovak National Museum**'s history exhibition and a terrace over the Danube, Austria and Hungary at once.
itinerary.evening: Across the **Most SNP** to the **UFO** observation deck on its single pylon, 95 m up, for the sunset over Petržalka and the river. Then back for beer at **Bratislavský meštiansky pivovar** on Drevená [VERIFY: current UFO deck admission].

itinerary.title: Petržalka, Slavín and Devín
itinerary.morning: **Petržalka**, seriously and not as a joke: built 1973–85, around 100,000 people in prefabricated *paneláky*, and by population density **the densest housing district in Central Europe**. Walk the Chorvátske rameno waterway, look at the colour repainting and the mature trees, and note that it works — full services, a tram-line extension, and low crime. It is the most instructive hour in the city.
itinerary.afternoon: Back over the river to **Slavín**, the Soviet war memorial and cemetery on the hill above the embassy quarter — 6,845 Red Army dead from the 1945 battle for the city, and the best panorama in Bratislava.
itinerary.evening: Bus 29 to **Devín**, the castle on the cliff at the **Morava–Danube confluence**, a Great Moravian stronghold and later a hard Iron Curtain frontier. Dinner back in town at the **Slovak Pub** on Obchodná — *bryndzové halušky*, *pirohy*, long wooden tables.

itinerary.title: East, by train
itinerary.morning: The **IC to Košice** from Bratislava hlavná stanica. Watch the country change: Danubian lowland, then the Váh valley, then the Tatras on the northern horizon around Poprad, then the eastern hills.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Košice and walk straight out onto **Hlavná ulica**. Get your bearings around the **singing fountain** and its adjacent musical clock, in the park in front of the cathedral.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at **Med Malina** on Hlavná — Slovak and Polish country cooking in a cellar, and the most reliably good meal in the city.

itinerary.title: The Gothic day
itinerary.morning: The **Cathedral of St Elisabeth**, begun around 1378: **the largest church in Slovakia** and **the easternmost Gothic cathedral in Europe**, with Rákóczi's crypt below and a north tower you can climb. Next door, St Michael's Chapel and the Urban Tower.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Lower Gate (Dolná brána)** — an archaeological undercroft beneath Hlavná preserving the medieval city gate, bastion and waterway, entered from the street. Then **Miklušova väznica**, the Miklós Prison, a pair of 15th-century houses converted into a jail and now a museum with the cells and torture chamber intact [VERIFY: current Lower Gate and Miklušova väznica hours and tickets].
itinerary.evening: **Rosto** for grilled meat and a good wine list. Slovak wine from the Tokaj slopes on the Hungarian border is the local pour and worth ordering.

itinerary.title: Spiš Castle and Levoča
itinerary.morning: East Slovak Museum first, if you have not yet: the **Košice Gold Treasure** — 2,920 gold coins, three gold medals and a Renaissance chain, walled up in the 17th century and found by chance in 1935, the largest hoard of its kind in Europe [VERIFY: current East Slovak Museum hours and Gold Treasure display].
itinerary.afternoon: Then west by train or car to **Spiš Castle (Spišský hrad)** — UNESCO-listed, and **one of the largest castle complexes in Central Europe** at over four hectares, standing on a travertine hill with nothing around it. Pair it with **Levoča**, the walled Spiš town whose Church of St James holds the world's tallest late-Gothic wooden altarpiece, carved by Master Pavol around 1517. *(Alternative: the **Slovak Karst** caves — Domica, Gombasek, Ochtinská Aragonite — also UNESCO, and closer.)*
itinerary.evening: Back to Košice. A late dinner at **Villa Cassa**, the city's most serious kitchen, in a restored townhouse.

itinerary.title: The last of Košice
itinerary.morning: The **Kunsthalle / Hala umenia** in the converted 1960s swimming hall on Rumanova — Slovakia's first purpose-built contemporary art institution outside Bratislava, and a good corrective to a week of Gothic.
itinerary.afternoon: Hlavná's courtyards, the Executioner's Bastion, the State Theatre, and the shops on Mlynská. Buy Slovak Tokaj and *bryndza* to take home.
itinerary.evening: Fly out of Košice (KSC), or take the night or evening IC back west. Košice airport is 6 km from the centre and the taxi is ten minutes.

accommodationStrategy.name: A hotel on Panská or Ventúrska
accommodationStrategy.description: puts you inside the pedestrian core, so all three Bratislava days start on foot and the airport coach drop at Most SNP is a five-minute walk. The trade-off is Friday and Saturday night noise — ask for a courtyard room.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; Bratislava rates spike for Vienna-overflow weekends [VERIFY: current nightly rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: A guesthouse or apartment near Šafárikovo námestie
accommodationStrategy.description: the cheaper, quieter alternative ten minutes from Hlavné námestie, with a tram stop, the Blue Church five minutes away and the Danube embankment at the end of the street. Better value than the old-town core by a third.

accommodationStrategy.name: A hotel on or just off Hlavná
accommodationStrategy.description: everything in Košice is on this one square, so anywhere on it removes transport from the equation entirely; the station is a ten-minute walk east for the Spiš day trip. Košice room rates run well below Bratislava's for the same standard.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 weeks ahead, except during the Košice Peace Marathon weekend in early October, when the city fills.

logistics.connectivity: Excellent 4G/5G in both cities and on the IC train. Free wi-fi in most cafés and on many DPB and DPMK vehicles.
logistics.emergency: **112**. Pharmacies are *lekáreň*; each city has a rotating night duty pharmacy posted on the door.
logistics.weather: Bratislava is Pannonian — hot summers, humid, with real thunderstorms; Košice sits lower and further east and gets colder winters and drier summers. Winter fog on the Danube can close the UFO deck's views for days.
logistics.bookingWindows: Hotels 2–6 weeks. The Bratislava–Košice IC seat 1–2 weeks. Slovak Philharmonic and Slovak National Theatre 2–4 weeks. Everything else takes walk-ins.
logistics.money: **Slovakia uses the euro**, and card acceptance is near-universal in both cities, including on ticket machines and in most restaurants. Carry €40–€60 in cash for market stalls, church donation boxes and the smaller Spiš-area sites.
logistics.transportRules: IDS BK and DPMK tickets must be **validated on boarding** — inspectors are frequent and the fine is immediate and cash-or-card on the spot. Luggage over a certain size needs its own ticket on Bratislava transport. The **Vienna airport coach** is the better arrival than BTS; it is also the better departure, running through the night.
logistics.permits: No permits needed. Photography is restricted inside the Blue Church during services and in parts of the East Slovak Museum's treasury. Drones are prohibited over both city centres and over Spiš Castle.

proTips: **Fly to Vienna.** The coach to Bratislava takes an hour and costs less than most airport transfers, and Vienna offers ten times the route choice. Book the return leg with enough slack for a border-queue delay.
Visit the **Blue Church at 08:00 on a weekday**, before the tour groups and while the low light is coming through the east windows. It is a parish church first and a monument second.
Give **Petržalka** two hours and cross on foot over the Most SNP or the Starý most. Understanding it is the difference between having seen Bratislava and having seen its postcard.
Take the **IC east on a weekday morning** and buy the seat reservation online; the Friday-afternoon service is full of students going home and there is no standing room worth having for five hours.
Eat off Hlavná in Košice, not on it. Terraces on the square carry a premium; the same kitchens' side-street rooms are 20–30% cheaper.
Do **Spiš Castle before 10:00 or after 16:00** in high summer — it is fully exposed, there is no shade on the upper ward, and the mid-afternoon heat on that travertine hill is punishing.
Learn *"Prosím si..."* (I'd like...) and *"Zaplatím, prosím"* (the bill, please). Slovak service warms noticeably to the attempt, and in Košice a *"köszönöm"* also lands well.

raw.Walkable blocks — Bratislava: The **Staré Mesto** is small enough to cross in fifteen minutes: **Michalská and Ventúrska** (the axis through Michael's Gate, the only surviving city gate), **Hlavné námestie** and **Františkánske námestie**, **Panská** and **Laurinská** for shops, **Kapitulská** — the quietest and oldest street, running to the cathedral — and **Židovská** and **Beblavého** climbing the castle hill. Across the river, **Petržalka** is a different exercise entirely, best walked along the Chorvátske rameno and the Sad Janka Kráľa park.
raw.Walkable blocks — Košice: Essentially one: **Hlavná ulica**, a 1.2 km spindle-shaped square that widens around the cathedral and narrows at each end, with **Mlynská**, **Alžbetina** and **Hlavná's** courtyards branching off. Everything in this itinerary except the East Slovak Museum's annexes is on or within 200 m of it.
raw.Transit passes and fares — Bratislava: The city network is **DPB** (buses, trolleybuses, trams), integrated into the regional **IDS BK** zone system. Bratislava city is **zones 100 + 101**; a ticket priced for those two zones covers everything you will use, including the bus to Devín. Fares are time-based rather than per-journey — short (about 15 minutes), standard (about 30), and longer bands, plus **24-hour, 72-hour and 7-day** passes, with the multi-day passes clearly the better buy from day one. Buy at machines, at kiosks, or in the IDS BK app; **validate paper tickets on boarding** [VERIFY: current IDS BK zone 100+101 single and multi-day fares].
raw.Transit passes and fares — Košice: **DPMK** runs trams, trolleybuses and buses; the tram loop around the centre and the lines out to the East Slovak Museum's Rodošto and the suburbs are the useful ones. Tickets are time-banded (roughly 30 and 60 minutes) with day passes available, and are cheaper than Bratislava's. Košice is compact enough that most visitors buy two or three singles across the whole stay [VERIFY: current DPMK fares and day-pass price].
raw.The train — and how long this country is: The **Bratislava–Košice IC** is the country's flagship service and it takes **about 5 h 20 to 6 h**, roughly 445 km via Trnava, Žilina, Poprad-Tatry and Prešov. There is no faster option; the alternative is a 1-hour flight. Book the IC seat in advance — it is reservation-based — and take a window on the right heading east for the High Tatras between Ružomberok and Poprad [VERIFY: current ZSSK IC fare and reservation rules].
raw.Cultural booking timelines: Very little in Slovakia genuinely sells out. The exceptions: the **Blue Church**, which is a working parish and open to visitors only in narrow windows around services; **Spiš Castle** in July–August, where the car park rather than the ticket office is the constraint; and any **Slovak Philharmonic** or **Slovak National Theatre** performance in Bratislava, which needs 2–4 weeks. Museums here take walk-ins.
raw.Architectural focal points and periods: **Gothic**: St Elisabeth's in Košice (14th–15th c.), St Martin's Cathedral in Bratislava, Levoča's St James with the Master Pavol altar. **Baroque**: the **Primate's Palace** (1778–81, Melchior Hefele) and the Pálffy and Esterházy town palaces that give the Staré Mesto its street walls. **Hungarian Secession**: **Ödön Lechner's Church of St Elizabeth — the Blue Church** (1909–13), the purest thing he built, with its blue-glazed Zsolnay ceramics and rolled parapet. **Czechoslovak functionalism**: the **Manderla** tower on Námestie SNP (1935), Bratislava's first high-rise and the emblem of the interwar republic. **Socialist modernism**: the **UFO** on the Most SNP (1972) and Petržalka itself.
